objective: Overseeing AI/ML model technique and algorithm selection: supervised/unsupervised/reinforcement learning tradeoffs against complexity and interpretability
secondaryObjectives: Overseeing model QA/QC: testing protocols, configuration management, and peer review of model design
Verifying data quality and readiness for training with a go/no-go decision, and verifying model readiness for operationalization

sources.cite: PMI Certified Professional in Managing AI (PMI-CPMAI) Examination Content Outline (September 2025): Responsible and Trustworthy AI 15%, Business Needs and Solutions 26%, Data Needs 26%, Model Development and Evaluation 16%, Operationalize 17%
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch of a training provider's syllabus page that restates the outline in its own words (PMI's PDF did not come up in search). Restated: data evaluation (assess data quality; analyze distributions for bias or gaps; exploratory data analysis); model governance (lifecycle management, versioning and change control, monitor performance and detect drift). The objective wording here is the course seed's; PMI's own wording is to verify. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's loan-data-bias-pmicpmai (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

The organization, the project, the figures and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You manage the AI project at a fictional credit union building a model to recommend small-loan decisions. Members who are declined must get reasons.
handover: The team proposes a deep neural network; a gradient-boosted tree and a logistic regression are close behind.
Regulation requires adverse-action reasons for declined applicants.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each review; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Week 2: compliance blocks the launch: declined members can't be told why.
Week 3: an outside review finds the model declines one postcode area's applicants at twice the rate; it wasn't tested.
Week 4: members in the affected area complain to the regulator.

algoPrompt.title: Accuracy or explanation?

choices.label: Require out-of-time testing, fairness tests by protected group, versioned data and model configuration, and a peer review of the design

choices.label: Accept the single split
choices.feedback: Untested over time and across groups.

scoring.modelReasoning: Overseeing model development means choosing techniques that balance performance with interpretability and the use case's requirements, requiring QA (testing protocols, fairness tests, configuration management, peer review), and making go/no-go decisions on readiness from evidence.
